To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified genes associated with susceptibility or resistance to periodontal disease by gene expression profiling in mice.
we have identified a set of genes that may be involved in the genetic susceptibility or resistance of alveolar periodontitis in mice.
quantitative gene expression profiling of the gingiva and spleen implicates genes for susceptibility and resistance to alveolar loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular basis for susceptibility and resistance to alveolar destruction in periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease that is one of the leading causes of tooth loss and a major cause of edentulism in the United States.
the genetic and molecular mechanisms of periodontal disease.

the identification of genes involved in the pathogenesis of periodontal disease and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the genetically determined susceptibility to and resistance against alveolar bone destruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of genes associated with susceptibility and resistance to alveolar loss is different in the susceptible and resistant strains.

the genetic basis for the resistance of the A/J mouse strain to alveolar loss is associated with the differential expression of Il15 and Selp genes, whereas the susceptibility of BALB/cByj mice to alveolar resorption is associated with the higher expression of Il1b, Tnfa, and Stat6.

this work provides a novel and sensitive method for quantitative gene expression profiling in a complex biological system and demonstrates that this method can be used to identify genes involved in susceptibility and resistance to alveolar periodontitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic basis of periodontal disease is complex.

susceptibility to periodontitis is associated with increased expression of proinflammatory mediators, whereas resistance is associated with increased production of immune mediators and decreased expression of proinfl ammatory mediators.

the susceptibility to alveolar periodontal bone loss is associated with increased expression of genes for inflammation and immune responses, while the resistance is associated with increased gene expression for innate and adaptive immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of genes associated with susceptibility or resistance to alveolar loss is detectable before the onset of disease.

the genetic susceptibility to periodontal bone loss is associated with increased expression of genes involved in inflammation, and the genetic resistance is associated with increased levels of genes that regulate the inflammatory response.
the genes that we identified are associated with the susceptibility to periodontal disease and that these genes can be used to predict the susceptibility to periodontoal disease.
